question: What is Activity Based Costing (ABC)? Explain the stages in its use and the benefits it offers.
sources: Activity based costing method: activities, cost pools and cost drivers

points.label: Meaning
points.description: ABC first assigns overheads to activities and then charges them to products or services according to how much of each activity they use.

points.label: Cost driver
points.description: A cost driver is the factor that causes the cost of an activity, for example number of set-ups, purchase orders or inspections.

points.label: Stages
points.description: Identify the main activities, collect their costs in cost pools, choose a cost driver for each pool, work out a rate per unit of driver, and charge products using their actual use of drivers.
points.basis: ABC: stages in applying activity based costing

points.label: Benefits
points.description: Gives more accurate product costs where overheads are large and products differ, supports better pricing and product-mix decisions, and shows activities that add no value so they can be cut.
points.basis: ABC: benefits of activity based costing
